newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris to mobilise 7,000 police for Pope visit.
newsitem.headline: Paris to mobilise 7,000 police for Pope visit.

text.p: Paris will mobilise about 7,000 police to assure order when Pope John Paul II visits France on August 21-24, the capital's police chief said on Monday.
Philippe Massoni told journalists there had been no threats against the Roman Catholic leader, whose visit has already incited protests from critics of his strict anti-abortion stand.
But Massoni said the pope was a head of state who merited special protection.

Church organisers of the visit, the Pope's sixth to France, expect up to 650,000 faithful to attend a Mass John Paul will celebrate in the Bois de Boulogne park in western Paris on the final day of his stay.
About 250,000 pilgrims were expected to arrive in Paris from abroad and other parts of France to take part in the World Youth Days the Church is running at the same time as the papal visit.
Massoni said security forces would include both normal police and riot police, 208 soldiers, anti-terrorist commandos and bomb disposal experts.

The police expect 4,000 buses to converge for the Pope's Sunday Mass at Longchamp racetrack in the Bois de Boulogne -- enough to cause a traffic jam 60 km (40 miles) long if lined up bumper-to-bumper.
